subject: Author guide — Dr. B. R. Ambedkar

guide.name: Dr. B. R. Ambedkar
guide.genre: Social Philosophy, Law, Economics & Political Thought
guide.bio: Bhimrao Ramji Ambedkar was an economist, jurist, constitutional thinker, and leader of the anti-caste movement in India. He chaired the Constituent Assembly's Drafting Committee and wrote extensively on caste, political representation, democracy, monetary economics, and Buddhism.
guide.autobiography: Waiting for a Visa (autobiographical episodes; written in the 1930s, published posthumously); see also his speeches and correspondence in the collected Writings and Speeches.
guide.startBook: Begin with Annihilation of Caste (1936) for his critique of caste hierarchy and social reform; then read Castes in India: Their Mechanism, Genesis and Development (1916) to encounter his earlier comparative analysis.
middleWorks: Who Were the Shudras? (1946) and The Untouchables (1948) — historical arguments about caste, to be studied critically alongside subsequent scholarship.
States and Minorities (1947) and selected Constituent Assembly speeches — political safeguards, rights, constitutional design and social democracy.
The Problem of the Rupee: Its Origin and Its Solution (1923) — currency, monetary institutions and Ambedkar's early economic research.
Thoughts on Linguistic States (1955) and Pakistan or the Partition of India (revised 1940s editions) — nationhood, language, federalism and minority representation.
guide.endBook: Conclude with The Buddha and His Dhamma (published posthumously in 1957), alongside Buddha or Karl Marx and selected late speeches, to examine Ambedkar's Navayāna Buddhist ethical and social philosophy.
guide.translationGuide: Edition Guide: Most major prose works were originally written in English. Compare accessible standalone editions with the Government of Maharashtra / Dr. Ambedkar Foundation's Dr. Babasaheb Ambedkar: Writings and Speeches volumes. Note original dates, later revisions, and editorial differences; The Buddha and His Dhamma was published posthumously.
guide.companionBooks: For autobiography, read Waiting for a Visa; for biography and context consult Eleanor Zelliot, Ambedkar's World; Christophe Jaffrelot, Dr Ambedkar and Untouchability; and Aakash Singh Rathore, Becoming Babasaheb. Compare later caste scholarship and constitutional interpretations rather than treating any one interpretation as conclusive.
